questions: Should the function read the entire file content into memory at once (as in the reference solution) or use incremental hashing to handle very large files?
Is the function required to handle symbolic links, or should it follow them to the target file's content?
Should the function normalize line endings (e.g., CRLF vs LF) or other text encodings before hashing, or treat files strictly as binary?
Are there any specific performance or memory constraints, such as a maximum file size the function must handle?
Should the function close files immediately after reading, or is it acceptable to keep them open until the end of the function?
If an I/O error occurs during reading (e.g., permission denied), should the function raise the original exception or a generic one?
Should the function compute the hash of empty files (zero bytes) and treat two empty files as identical?
Is the function expected to handle concurrent modifications to the files while reading, or assume files are static during execution?
